Definition: The country's performance on the WIPO Global Innovation Index (GII), which measures innovation capabilities across institutions, human capital, infrastructure, market sophistication, business sophistication, knowledge outputs, and creative outputs. Provides a composite view of the national innovation ecosystem.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: DR Congo is not among the 133 economies ranked in WIPO's GII 2024 (confirmed via the report's alphabetical economy index, which skips from Colombia/Costa Rica with no Congo entry, and via the absence of a country profile at wipo.int/edocs/gii-ranking/2024/cd.pdf, unlike other African states such as Benin, Cameroon or Angola). The original 'rank 121+' claim had no source and is unsupported. Recalculated to 0 (not included in GII), the scale's explicit option for excluded economies.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Partech data (reported by TechCabal, June 2023) show the DRC start-up ecosystem raised $38m in 2022, but 98% of this went to a single firm (Web3 company Jambo's $30m Series A); excluding that outlier, activity is minimal — Tuma's $500,000 round in 2023 was reported as the largest-ever fintech raise in the country. This confirms 'Emerging', with concentrated, thin funding and no more than a couple of active hubs (Silikin Village, KivuTech); no evidence found of sustained $50m+ annual VC activity that would justify a higher score. Value Code confirmed at 2.

Definition: The number and activity level of technology hubs, incubators, accelerators, and co-working spaces focused on technology and innovation. These provide physical infrastructure and support for tech entrepreneurship and skills development.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Briter Intelligence's DRC directory (published April 2026, with the International Trade Centre and FCDO) maps at least ten active entrepreneur-support/tech hubs (including Silikin Village, Ingenious City, LUBA Hub, Kobo Hub, Centre d'innovation de Lubumbashi, KIVU Impact Center), corroborated by AfriLabs' separate country listing (KivuTech, Ovation, Wito XR Studio, Diambilay Business Center) and other named hubs (Lumumba Lab, GoHubDRC). This is well above the '1-2 hubs' claim; recalculated to 4 (10-24 hubs with diverse focus areas).

Definition: The scale and quality of tertiary-level ICT and STEM education programmes available in the country, based on the number and quality of institutions offering ICT degrees, computer science programmes, and engineering courses relative to the population.
Value Name: Very limited (<2 institutions with ICT programmes)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Multiple institutions offering dedicated computer science/ICT degree programmes were verified, including the Université de Kinshasa Polytechnic's Génie Informatique department (est. 2005, with AI/software/network labs), Université Kongo's Faculté des Sciences Informatiques, ISIG's Master en Sciences Informatiques (Goma), and UWB Congo's Faculté des Sciences Informatiques & IA. This directly contradicts the '<2 institutions' claim. No enrolment figures or quality rankings (QS, UNESCO UIS graduate counts) were found, so the code is conservatively recalculated to 3 (Moderate: several institutions, growing enrolment) rather than higher.
